born.name: Willis Carrier
born.short: The American engineer who taught buildings to breathe
bio: In 1902 the young American engineer designed the first modern air-conditioning system, to control the humidity in a Brooklyn printing works.
He went on to found the Carrier company, and his invention transformed cinemas, offices, factories and homes around the world.
Few inventions have changed where – and how – people live and work quite so much.

born.name: Charles M. Schulz
born.short: Gave the world Charlie Brown and Snoopy
bio: Born in Minneapolis, he launched the Peanuts comic strip in 1950, introducing the world to Charlie Brown, Snoopy and the gang.
He wrote and drew almost 18,000 strips himself over nearly fifty years, and at its peak Peanuts appeared in thousands of newspapers worldwide.
He died in 2000, the night before his final Sunday strip was published.

born.name: Tina Turner
bio: Born Anna Mae Bullock in Tennessee, she found fame in the 1960s with Ike & Tina Turner and the classic River Deep – Mountain High.
Her solo comeback with the 1984 album Private Dancer made her a global superstar, and The Best became an anthem across Britain.
She later made her home in Switzerland and became a Swiss citizen. She died in 2023, aged 83.

born.name: John McVie
bio: Born in Ealing, London, he joined Fleetwood Mac in its first year, 1967 – and his surname gave the band the “Mac” in its name.
His bass lines anchor Rumours, one of the best-selling albums of all time.
He and drummer Mick Fleetwood are the only members to have been with the band from the very start.

born.name: Rita Ora
born.short: From Pristina to the top of the charts
bio: Born in Pristina, in what is now Kosovo, she moved to London with her family when she was a baby.
Her first UK number one came in 2012 with Hot Right Now, alongside DJ Fresh, and many more hits followed.
She has also become a familiar face on television, including judging on The Voice UK and The X Factor.

born.name: Danny Welbeck
bio: The Manchester-born striker came through the Manchester United academy and won the Premier League with the club.
He later played for Arsenal, Watford and Brighton, and won 42 England caps.
In August 2026, aged 35, he joined Chelsea on a two-year deal.

remembered.name: John Loudon McAdam
remembered.short: The Scot who gave us “macadam” roads
bio: Born in Ayr, Scotland, he developed a new way of building roads from layers of small, broken stones.
His “macadam” roads were smoother, drier and longer-lasting than anything before them, and spread around the world.
When tar was later added to bind the stones, the result gave us a word we still use every day: tarmac.

remembered.name: Sojourner Truth
bio: Born into slavery in New York State, she escaped to freedom with her baby daughter in 1826.
She became one of the most powerful speakers of her age, campaigning against slavery and for women’s rights.
Her 1851 speech in Akron, Ohio, remembered as “Ain’t I a Woman?”, is still quoted today.

remembered.name: Michael Bentine
bio: Born in Watford to a Peruvian father, he was one of the founders of The Goons, alongside Spike Milligan, Peter Sellers and Harry Secombe.
He left after the first series but went on to make the inventive TV comedy It’s a Square World.
A generation of children also knew him from his puppet show Potty Time.

remembered.name: Stephen Sondheim
remembered.short: The giant of the modern musical
bio: He wrote the lyrics for West Side Story and Gypsy before he was thirty.
He then wrote both words and music for shows including Company, Sweeney Todd and Into the Woods, and won a Pulitzer Prize for Sunday in the Park with George.
Widely seen as the greatest figure in modern musical theatre, he died aged 91.

history.head: The boy king’s tomb
history.body: Howard Carter and Lord Carnarvon enter the tomb of Tutankhamun in Egypt’s Valley of the Kings.

history.head: Here’s looking at you
history.body: Casablanca, starring Humphrey Bogart and Ingrid Bergman, has its premiere in New York.

history.head: The Brink’s-Mat robbery
history.body: Robbers raid a warehouse near Heathrow and escape with around £26 million in gold bullion.

history.head: Concorde’s last flight
history.body: The supersonic airliner makes its final ever flight, landing at Filton in Bristol.

sport.head: The NHL is born
sport.body: Ice hockey’s National Hockey League is founded in Montreal with five clubs.

sport.head: A first for South America
sport.body: In Tokyo, Argentina’s Pascual Pérez beats Yoshio Shirai to become world flyweight champion.

sport.head: Holmes v Cobb
sport.body: Larry Holmes keeps his WBC heavyweight title with a one-sided 15-round win over Randall “Tex” Cobb in Houston.
